requirements.statement: Each zone (<area> element) of an image map that carries information has a text alternative.

citations.quote: Chaque zone d’une image réactive (balise `<area>`) porteuse d’information a-t-elle une alternative textuelle ?
Vérifier que la zone réactive est pourvue au moins d’une alternative textuelle parmi les suivantes :

routes.statement: The zone's aria-label attribute gives the alternative.
The zone's alt attribute gives the alternative.

rationale.text: The test applies to zones that carry information, and whether a zone conveys information needed to understand its content is judgment. A zone in the glossary is a clickable or a non-clickable region of an image map. The methodology accepts two sources for an <area>: aria-label and alt; the glossary order lists <area> for no other source. Neither glossary note on images alone in a link or a button concerns an <area>, so the requirement has no exception. axe's area-alt examines only zones with an href inside a map, so non-clickable zones are never looked at, and its link is partial. It accepts aria-labelledby and a non-empty title as well, which this test does not list for <area>, so its clean result proves nothing. Its fault may land on a zone that carries no information, so it is evidence only; it also examines hidden zones (excludeHidden is off). A custom check that faults a clickable zone with no alt and no aria-label was considered and rejected. The wording of this test does not say that every clickable zone carries information, and the fault would rest on that. What would raise it: an official statement, in this test's text or its glossary, that a clickable zone always carries information. So the entry is none. Applicability is judgment: it depends on which zones carry information. Needs is empty: the methodology reads attributes.

citations.quote: Pour chaque élément `<area>`, déterminer si la zone réactive est porteuse d’information ;
Zone cliquable ou zone non cliquable d’une image réactive côté client
Image qui véhicule une information nécessaire à la compréhension du contenu auquel elle est associée.
Sinon, contenu de l’attribut alt pour les balises : ; ; .
